harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 with 7 compressed rotations and copytruncate (no live writer process was found, so copytruncate is the safe mechanism to let the app keep writing post-rotation). Verified end-to-end functionally, then completed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified config persistence, prior log data, timer activity, and rotation function post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: no live app process holds app.log open; logrotate 3.18.0 present; logrotate.timer active
Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Dry-run validated config syntax with logrotate -d
Forced rotation twice pre-restart, confirming inode preservation (copytruncate), .gz compression, and continued writability
Captured pre-restart boot_id and full healthy state (config, log dir, log content, timer status)
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1; acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again

Post-restart: verified config file persisted, prior log content intact, logrotate.timer active, and re-ran forced rotation to confirm inode-preserving copytruncate behavior still functions with continued writes and 7-rotation retention

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with 7 compressed rotations configured for /var/log/inventory/app.log
evidence.summary: Wrote and cat'd /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app showing daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate; logrotate -d dry-run confirmed valid syntax and correct rotation pattern matching.

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation (functional proof)
evidence.summary: Forced rotation twice: inode of app.log stayed 894710 across rotations (copytruncate truncates in place rather than replacing the file), and new writes after each rotation landed correctly in the live app.log while old content was compressed to app.log.1.gz / .2.gz.
Captured boot_id 6aa805ba-5845-488d-af03-a621555936e2, confirmed logrotate config present, log dir state with prior rotations, and logrotate.timer active.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent polls timed out/reset while node was down; exec succeeded again with boot_id 79f223b0-9008-4475-a38a-0adadc6604f8, proving an actual reboot occurred (not just a service restart).

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of log rotation setup and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, logrotate config file, prior rotated .gz files, and the pre-reboot log marker were all intact; logrotate.timer was active again; a fresh forced rotation confirmed copytruncate still preserves the inode and allows continued writes, with rotation count still capped via rotate 7.
